archetype.name: Fringe Contender (all offense)
archetype.definition: A Dallas team with a top-ten offense and a bottom-two defense, good enough to outscore most of the league but too leaky to beat good teams reliably, kept in the race mostly by a soft NFC East.

report.headline: Top-six offense, 31st defense: a coin-flip team losing the close ones.
report.take:
If this season feels familiar, it should. Last year's Cowboys ranked 5th in offensive EPA and 32nd in defensive EPA allowed. This year's rank 6th and 31st. Dak Prescott has started every game, the offense scores 27.3 points a game (6th), and the defense gives back 26.2 (25th). Net EPA sits exactly at league average, 17th, with a point differential of +10. That is a .500 team by construction, not by accident. The defensive collapse that started in 2024 has not been fixed. It has been outgunned.

The 4-5 record is a little worse than the play. The point differential implies 5.5 wins, wins over expected is -1.45 (26th), and three of the losses came by a field goal or less: Baltimore 31-34, Arizona 30-33, and the 20-28 opener at New York was close until late. The losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay were different. In those the offense coughed up three and two turnovers and produced negative passing EPA, the only two games all year it did. When Prescott protects the ball, this offense has scored at least 27 in every game since week 2 except those two.

The defense's problem is not big plays through the air. Deep-ball EPA allowed ranks 8th. It is everything underneath and on the ground. Offenses pass four points less often than normal against Dallas (29th), because running works: rush EPA allowed is 30th, and Tampa Bay (28th in offense) ran for 241. The defense is last in third-down rate at 48.3% and 25th in red-zone touchdown rate, so drives that should end in punts or field goals end in sevens. Opposing WR1s score 6.8 PPR points over their norm, the worst mark in the league. Penalties (8.2 a game, 26th, including 153 yards at Indianapolis) add free yards on top.

Where it goes depends on the calendar more than any fix. San Francisco comes to town, then Tennessee (1-7) and Philadelphia (2-7) at home, then a December run of Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville, all top-five defenses. New York leads the division at 5-2-1 with two Giants-Cowboys meetings still to come. Nothing here suggests the defense improves, especially with Joey Porter Jr., P.J. Locke, DeMarvion Overshown and Malachi Lawrence all sidelined. This is a shootout team that needs its close-game luck to even out.

strengths.title: Efficient, well-protected passing game
strengths.body: Passing EPA ranks 7th and the line allows sacks on just 3.8% of dropbacks (5th), so Prescott rarely takes drive-killing losses. It rests on a quarterback and protection that have held up all nine games, not on a hot streak. Last year's offense ranked 5th too, which makes it the most bankable part of the team. The catch is that George Pickens and Jake Ferguson are both out, which concentrates even more on CeeDee Lamb, already at 108 targets.

strengths.title: A run game better than its YPC
strengths.body: At 3.79 yards a carry (19th), the ground game looks pedestrian. Its EPA and success rate both rank 8th, though, so it stays on schedule and avoids negative plays. Javonte Williams carries the load, and the 204- and 179-yard games against Philadelphia and Indianapolis show it can take over against weak fronts. With Tyler Goodson out for multiple weeks, depth behind Williams is thin.

strengths.title: Fourth-down aggression
strengths.body: Dallas goes for it in every situation the model calls a go, the highest rate in the league. For an offense this efficient and a defense this porous, extending possessions is the right bet. It is a coaching choice and should last.

concerns.title: A defense that can't get off the field
concerns.body: Opponents convert 48.3% of third downs, last in the league, and score touchdowns on 67.6% of red-zone trips. Long drives that finish in the end zone are why 31st-ranked EPA allowed turns into 26 points a game. It is not a small-sample blip: the 2025 unit was 32nd. The injury list now includes the top corner, a starting safety and two linebackers, so it is more likely to get worse than better.

concerns.title: Run funnel, and lead receivers feast
concerns.body: Offenses lean on the run against Dallas more than almost anyone, because rush EPA allowed is 30th and explosive runs allowed rank 23rd. Through the air, opposing WR1s run 6.8 PPR points above their usual output, worst in the league, while WR2s are held under. The coverage can't handle the best receiver, and the front can't stop the run. That leaves no easy way to call a defense.

concerns.title: Self-inflicted turnovers and flags
concerns.body: The two clear losses, to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, came with three and two giveaways and the only negative passing-EPA games of the year. The team also ranks 26th in penalties per game. This is a correctable but recurring flaw. Even in the week 9 win, Dallas turned it over twice and was flagged for 153 yards.

trend.note: Wins and losses have nearly alternated all year. The offense has trended up lately, with 38, 30 and 27 points in the last three games and big rushing days against Philadelphia and Indianapolis. The defense is still giving up 30-plus to teams like Arizona.

nextGame.headline: Both secondaries banged up; Dallas needs a shootout to win.
nextGame.body:
San Francisco is the league's best team by net EPA. It has the No. 1 passing offense, the best pass protection by sack rate, and the No. 1 run defense by EPA. That last part matters most for Dallas: Williams's efficient running is unlikely to carry the day, so the game falls on Prescott. He should have time, since the 49ers have only 15 sacks (27th) and Dallas allows few. The Book has San Francisco by 3.5 with a 55.5 total, Dallas +170. That total reads as an expected shootout, and it puts Dallas's 31st-ranked defense against the best offense it has seen. San Francisco's 7-1 has a little air in it: perfect in one-score games, +1.91 wins over expected, and last in special-teams EPA.

Availability cuts both ways. Dallas is without Pickens, Ferguson, backup TE Luke Schoonmaker, KaVontae Turpin and Goodson on offense. On defense it is missing Porter Jr., Locke, Overshown and Lawrence, with Donovan Ezeiruaku day-to-day. San Francisco is just as thin at receiver: Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans are out, Christian Kirk is on IR, and Brandon Aiyuk is on a roster exemption. It has also lost DT Gracen Halton for the season, and its two starting corners, Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir, are both day-to-day. The early forecast shows gusts near 25 mph, but the stadium has a retractable roof that is likely to be closed, so the weather shouldn't decide anything.

waysToWin.title: Throw on a thinned, low-pressure secondary
waysToWin.body: If Green or Lenoir can't go, San Francisco's coverage loses its two every-down corners, with Nate Hobbs also not activated. The 49ers already leak against third receivers (0.58 EPA a target, 28th) and don't generate sacks, so a clean pocket should give Prescott time to work Lamb and the depth receivers. This is Dallas's most reliable path, because it plays to the offense's best unit.

waysToWin.title: Steal hidden yards on special teams
waysToWin.body: San Francisco ranks last in special-teams EPA, losing field position every week. Dallas is neutral there, so in a projected shootout a couple of short fields could be the margin. Turpin's absence blunts the return game somewhat.

waysToWin.title: Keep it close, go for it late
waysToWin.body: The 49ers haven't lost a one-score game, and their win total runs almost two ahead of their scoring margin, a run of fortune that tends to cool. If Dallas keeps it within a score into the fourth quarter, its league-leading fourth-down aggression gives it extra possessions to flip the result.

waysToLose.title: Purdy picks apart the defense
waysToLose.body: San Francisco's passing EPA is the best in the league and its protection allows the fewest sacks. Dallas ranks 29th in pass EPA allowed and 23rd in sack rate, so there is little hope of pressure bailing out the coverage. Even with a depleted receiver room, a 49ers offense that converts third downs against the league's worst third-down defense can end this by the third quarter.

waysToLose.title: Run game stalls, offense goes one-dimensional
waysToLose.body: The 49ers allow the lowest rush EPA and the fewest explosive runs in the league, and Goodson's injury leaves Williams with little help. If the run is shut off, Dallas faces obvious passing downs against a defense with 13 takeaways (5th). That is the same script as the Tampa Bay loss, where three turnovers sank the night.

waysToLose.title: Flags hand San Francisco free drives
waysToLose.body: Dallas ranks 26th in penalties per game, while San Francisco ranks 6th. Against a defense that already can't get off the field, defensive flags on third down turn stops into touchdowns. Against an offense this efficient, there is no margin to absorb them.

nextGame.watch: Whether Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir suit up. If either sits, Dallas's best path to an upset opens through Lamb against a backup corner.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the real thing. It was top-five last year and is top-ten again, and Tennessee and Philadelphia should allow it to pile up points before a December gauntlet of top-five defenses in Seattle, Los Angeles and Jacksonville. The defense is the real thing in the other direction, two straight seasons near the bottom, and the current injury list strips out its best corner and two linebackers. Some close-loss bad luck should even out, which is worth maybe a win over the stretch, but this is not a team built to string together wins against good opponents.

The path to January runs through the division. The two late Giants games and a trip to Washington matter more than the marquee matchups. Expect something close to a .500 finish, with the NFC East title realistic only if Dallas sweeps the soft November games and takes at least one from New York.
swingFactors: Returns of Porter Jr., Locke and Overshown
Prescott's turnover rate against December's top defenses

confidence.note: Nine games, but the profile matches 2025 almost exactly; the injuries on both sides of the ball are the wild card.
